newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian bourse active, index up nearly one pct.
newsitem.headline: Estonian bourse active, index up nearly one pct.

text.p: The Estonian stock exchange saw active trade on Thursday and most shares gained, dealers said.
Volume on the main list came to 9.8 million kroons after 6.99 million kroons and the Tallinn stock exchange index rose 0.99 percent to 98.92.
"Shares were undervalued after the summer but I think that now they will go up to a certain level and stay there rather than fall back," said Charlie Viikberg, trader at Savings Bank.
He said activity should also be positive next week as the market is looking forward to nine-month results from the banks.
Today's share gains were led by Hansapank, which rose above 100 kroons for the first time since the spring.
It ended at 99.55 kroons, having at one point reached 100.15 kroons, and turned over 1.62 million kroons. It closed at 98.25 kroons on Wednesday.
Most active on the official list was Forexbank, which traded 4.8 million kroons and rose to 77.85 kroons from 76.25.
Computer firm Pennu became the market's first hi-tech stock as it made its debut on the exchange's new second-tier list for small and medium-sized companies.
It rose from around 60 kroons to end today's business at 69.60 kroons on turnover of just over one million kroons.
The free market list turned over 5.4 million kroons and the Rakvere meat plant was again the most active on trade of more than two million kroons and ending at 4.05 kroons versus 3.82.
"Some people are taking a long-term view of the stock as last year it made a 17 million kroon loss. They are hoping for profit this year," Viikberg said.
Plastics factory Norma was active on 1.4 million kroons after yesterday's positive earnings figures and it rose to 23.40 kroons from 22.60.
